stories.title: The Little Elephant Who Shared
stories.synopsis: A gentle adventure about friendship, generosity, and discovering that sharing can make everyone happier.
stories.lesson: Sharing, generosity and caring for friends.
pages: Little Gaja the elephant lived at the edge of a green forest, where mango trees grew taller than the clouds.
One sunny morning he found a basket of ripe mangoes, golden and sweet. His tummy rumbled with joy.
Just as he lifted the first mango, he heard a tiny sniffle. Mina the mouse was sitting alone, far too small to reach the fruit.
Gaja thought for a moment. Then he smiled and set the basket down between them. There is plenty for two, he said.
They ate until their cheeks were sticky, and the whole forest agreed that mangoes taste best when they are shared.

stories.title: Aarav and the Magical Cricket Bat
stories.synopsis: Aarav finds a glowing cricket bat in the garden shed and learns that real magic is practice, patience and teamwork.
stories.lesson: Practice and teamwork matter more than any magic.
pages: Behind the garden shed, Aarav found an old cricket bat that glowed softly, like a lantern at dusk.
When he swung it, the ball floated up past the treetops and landed in the neighbour's courtyard. Everyone cheered.
But the next day the bat would not glow at all. Aarav felt his heart sink.
A wise old gardener smiled. Magic is only a spark, beta. The fire is your own practice and your friends beside you.
So Aarav practised every evening with his friends, and on match day the bat glowed again, brighter than ever.
Together they won, and Aarav never forgot who the real magic belonged to.

stories.title: Mira and the Moonlit Garden
stories.synopsis: When the moon rises, Mira discovers a quiet garden where flowers hum lullabies to help little ones fall asleep.
stories.lesson: Calm breaths and kind words help us rest.
pages: Mira could not sleep. So she tiptoed to the window and saw a silver path leading into the garden.
The jasmine flowers were humming a slow, sleepy song, and the fireflies swayed along to the tune.
Mira took a deep breath, then another, and her eyes grew heavy. The moon winked, and she drifted back to bed.

stories.title: The Banyan Tree's Secret
stories.synopsis: An old banyan tree in a village square holds a secret about patience, and one curious child is ready to listen.
stories.lesson: Good things grow slowly, with patience.
pages: In the middle of a village stood a banyan tree so old that nobody remembered who had planted it.
Little Kavya asked it, How did you grow so big? The leaves rustled, and she leaned in to listen.
I started as a seed no bigger than your fingernail, whispered the tree. Every day I grew a tiny bit, and that is all.
Kavya planted a seed that evening. She watered it patiently, and the banyan seemed to smile.

stories.title: Ananya's Journey to the Stars
stories.synopsis: Ananya builds a paper rocket and travels across the night sky, meeting planets who each teach her something new.
pages: Ananya loved the night sky. One evening she folded a paper rocket, whispered a wish, and it began to glow.
The rocket zoomed past the moon, which waved hello with a sleepy crater smile.
Next came Mars, red and dusty. Ask me anything, it boomed, and Ananya asked why it was red.
Saturn spun its rings like a giant hula hoop. Even the biggest rings are made of tiny pieces, it said, working together.
On Jupiter, a great storm rolled by. Storms are loud, said Jupiter, but they pass, and so do worries.
Far away, a comet left a sparkling trail. Ananya followed it until she could see the whole galaxy twinkling.
She felt small, and also very brave. Questions, she realised, were the fuel for her rocket.
The rocket drifted home, and Ananya fell asleep with starlight in her hair, already planning her next journey.

stories.title: The Lanterns of Jaipur
stories.synopsis: On the night of the festival, two siblings light a lantern for every neighbour and discover how light grows when it is shared.
stories.lesson: A small light grows when we share it.
pages: In Jaipur, the festival night was coming, and Riya and her brother Dev had only one lantern.
They lit it, then used its flame to light the neighbours' lanterns, one by one, until the whole street glowed pink and gold.
